new.title: Stand before the black basalt Diyarbakır City Walls
new.desc: The roughly 5.5 km ring of basalt walls around Sur dates mainly to the Roman and Byzantine eras and was extended by later Islamic dynasties. With the Hevsel Gardens, the walls were inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 2015.
new.tip: Free to see all day; the stretch at Dağ Kapı is the easiest to start from. Late afternoon light turns the basalt almost black and gold.
new.q: Diyarbakır Surları, Dağ Kapı, Sur, Diyarbakır

new.title: Explore İçkale and the Diyarbakır Archaeology Museum
new.desc: The Inner Castle (İçkale) in the north-east corner of the walled city holds the Diyarbakır Archaeology Museum, with finds spanning about 9,000 years of Mesopotamian history. The compound also contains the ruined Church of St George and a mansion used as an Atatürk museum.
new.tip: Open Tuesday to Sunday; the museum charges an entry fee while the outer castle grounds are free. Allow two hours.
new.q: Diyarbakır Arkeoloji Müzesi, İçkale, Sur, Diyarbakır

new.title: Enter the Great Mosque of Diyarbakır, Anatolia's oldest
new.desc: Ulu Cami was begun in 1091 under the Seljuk Malik-Shah and reuses Roman and Byzantine columns and capitals around a double-storey arcaded courtyard. Locals call it the fifth holy sanctuary after Mecca, Medina, Jerusalem and Damascus.
new.tip: Free; dress modestly and avoid prayer times. The sundial in the courtyard still keeps time.
new.q: Diyarbakır Ulu Camii, Gazi Caddesi, Sur, Diyarbakır

new.title: Step into Surp Giragos, the Middle East's largest Armenian church
new.desc: The church of St Giragos (Cyriacus) is thought to date to the 16th century and was reopened in 2011, damaged in the 2015-16 fighting in Sur, then restored by the state and reopened in May 2022. It is the largest Armenian church in the Middle East.
new.tip: Free; opening hours vary, so ask at the gate on Göçmen Sokak. Services are held on Sundays.
new.q: Surp Giragos Ermeni Kilisesi, Göçmen Sokak, Sur, Diyarbakır

new.title: Visit the restored Mar Petyun Chaldean Church
new.desc: The 17th-century Chaldean church in Sur is the only Chaldean church in Diyarbakır province. It was damaged in 2015, restored by the state by 2023 and reopened for worship with a priest after 108 years without one.
new.tip: Close to Surp Giragos, so visit both together; check at the gate for opening times.
new.q: Mar Petyun Keldani Kilisesi, Cemal Yılmaz Caddesi, Sur, Diyarbakır

new.title: See the Virgin Mary Syriac Orthodox Church
new.desc: Meryem Ana Kilisesi is the main church of Diyarbakır's small Syriac Orthodox community, a courtyard church thought to originate in the early Christian period. It stands on Uçak Sokak in the south-west of Sur.
new.tip: Open Tuesday to Sunday around 10:00-17:00 with a small admission fee; ring the bell if the gate is shut.
new.q: Meryem Ana Kilisesi, Uçak Sokak, Sur, Diyarbakır

new.title: Admire the striped stonework of Hasan Paşa Hanı
new.desc: Built in 1572-75 by the governor Hasan Pasha, the han is a two-storey caravanserai in alternating black basalt and white limestone bands. It stands across Gazi Caddesi from the Great Mosque and now houses breakfast places and craft shops.
new.tip: Free to enter during the day. Come early on weekends before the courtyard fills.
new.q: Hasan Paşa Hanı, Gazi Caddesi, Dabanoğlu, Sur, Diyarbakır

new.title: Rest in the courtyard of Sülüklü Han
new.desc: This 1620 caravanserai near the Great Mosque takes its name (leech inn) from a well in its courtyard once said to have leeches used for treatment. Its tree-shaded court holds cafés and shops.
new.tip: Open daily, free to walk in; a good place for a break after the Ulu Cami.
new.q: Sülüklü Han, Değer Sokak, Cami Kebir, Sur, Diyarbakır

new.title: Step into the poet Cahit Sıtkı Tarancı's house museum
new.desc: The 19th-century Diyarbakır mansion where the poet Cahit Sıtkı Tarancı (1910-1956) was born is now a house museum with his belongings and manuscripts. It shows a typical basalt courtyard house with a fine iwan.
new.tip: Reported open Tuesday to Sunday roughly 08:30-16:30; Turkish signage only. Confirm before going, as museum hours have changed.
new.q: Cahit Sıtkı Tarancı Müzesi, Cami Kebir, Sur, Diyarbakır

new.title: Visit the Ziya Gökalp house museum
new.desc: The house where the sociologist and poet Ziya Gökalp (1876-1924) was born in Diyarbakır is now a museum of his life and of period domestic life. It is a short walk west of the Great Mosque.
new.tip: Closed on Mondays, shut by about 16:30; ask at the door for current hours.
new.q: Ziya Gökalp Müzesi, Ziya Gökalp Mahallesi, Sur, Diyarbakır

new.title: Tour the Cemil Paşa Mansion, now the City Museum
new.desc: The Cemil Paşa Konağı was built in the late 1880s for the Cemilpaşazade family and restored as the Diyarbakır City Museum. It shows the city's history through documents, photographs and a typical Ottoman-era konak layout.
new.tip: Check hours before going; combine with İçkale, which is nearby.
new.q: Cemil Paşa Konağı, Sur, Diyarbakır

new.title: Look up at the Four-Legged Minaret
new.desc: The Şeyh Mutahhar Mosque, built in 1500-1530, is known for its minaret standing on four basalt columns, so that passers-by walk underneath it. It is the best-known mosque form in old Diyarbakır.
new.tip: Free and open around the clock from outside; the minaret stands on Yenikapı Sokak.
new.q: Dört Ayaklı Minare, Şeyh Mutahhar Camii, Savaş, Sur, Diyarbakır

new.title: See the striped Nebi Mosque and its Kurşunlu neighbour
new.desc: Nebi Camii in the Cami Nebi quarter is one of the Ottoman-period mosques of Sur built in the alternating black and white courses typical of Diyarbakır. It anchors a quiet residential corner of the old city.
new.tip: Free from outside; visit outside prayer times.
new.q: Nebi Camii, Cami Nebi, Sur, Diyarbakır

new.title: Visit the 1520 Kurşunlu Mosque in Sur
new.desc: The Kurşunlu (Fatih Paşa) Mosque dates from 1520 and is named for its lead-covered dome. It is an Ottoman mosque of the classical period within Sur.
new.tip: Free; open for visitors outside prayer times, daily from early morning to evening.
new.q: Kurşunlu Camii, Fatih Sokak, Sur, Diyarbakır

new.title: See Mardin Kapı and the Hazreti Ömer Mosque
new.desc: Mardin Kapı is the southern gate of the walls, beside the 12th-century Hazreti Ömer Mosque. The Nur and Keçi bastions stand nearby on the southern curve of the ramparts.
new.tip: Free; the gate area is a good start point for a walk along the south walls above the Hevsel Gardens.
new.q: Mardin Kapı, Sur, Diyarbakır

new.title: Look out from Keçi Burcu (Goat Tower) over the Tigris
new.desc: The Goat Tower is a bastion of the southern walls with a wide view over the Hevsel Gardens and the Tigris valley. One source notes it has been closed to the public in recent years, so it is best seen from the walls and gardens.
new.tip: Check whether access is open; the view is available from the nearby walk above the gardens.
new.q: Keçi Burcu, Sur, Diyarbakır

new.title: Stroll the Hevsel Gardens below the walls
new.desc: The roughly 300-hectare Hevsel Gardens between the walls and the Tigris have been cultivated for thousands of years and, with the walls, form a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Market gardens, orchards and fields run from Mardin Kapı to the Ten-Eyed Bridge.
new.tip: Free; go in the morning or at sunset, and wear shoes for dirt paths.
new.q: Hevsel Bahçeleri, Sur, Diyarbakır

new.title: Watch sunset from the Ten-Eyed Bridge over the Tigris
new.desc: The Ongözlü (Ten-Arched) Bridge crosses the Tigris south of the walled city and goes back to the 11th century, with later repairs. It has been a pedestrian bridge for years and the view of the river is best at dusk.
new.tip: Free; reach it by a walk down through the Hevsel Gardens or by car from the Mardin road.
new.q: On Gözlü Köprü, Sur, Diyarbakır

new.title: Take in the Tigris from Gazi Köşkü park
new.desc: Gazi Köşkü is a mansion in a riverside park overlooking the Tigris south of the old city, a popular place for locals to sit and picnic.
new.tip: Free; best in the evening when families gather.
new.q: Gazi Köşkü, Diyarbakır

new.title: Visit the Hz. Süleyman Mosque near İçkale
new.desc: The Hazreti Süleyman Mosque stands in a park by the Inner Castle, with an adjoining cemetery of Companions of the Prophet. It is named among the main sights of the old city.
new.tip: Free; walk down from İçkale.
new.q: Hz. Süleyman Camii, Cevat Paşa, Sur, Diyarbakır

new.title: See the Nasuh Paşa Mosque south of İçkale
new.desc: The Nasuh Paşa Mosque, built in 1619, is one of the later Ottoman mosques of Sur, built in the local black basalt and white limestone courses.
new.tip: Free; combine with İçkale and the Hz. Süleyman Mosque.
new.q: Nasuh Paşa Camii, Cevat Paşa, Sur, Diyarbakır

new.title: Listen to Kurdish stranan at the Dengbêj House
new.desc: The Dengbêj Evi in Sur is a venue where dengbêjs, traditional Kurdish singer-storytellers, perform epic songs and tales in their own language, with a tea garden. It keeps alive an oral tradition that long preceded written Kurdish.
new.tip: Ask locally for the day's session; no fixed schedule was confirmed, and the songs are in Kurdish.
new.q: Dengbêj Evi, Sur, Diyarbakır

new.title: Browse the Coppersmiths' Bazaar in Suriçi
new.desc: In the Bakırcılar Çarşısı craftsmen still hammer copper by hand in small workshops. It is one of the working trade lanes of the old city.
new.tip: Weekday mornings are busiest; bargain politely.
new.q: Bakırcılar Çarşısı, Cami Kebir, Sur, Diyarbakır

new.title: Have breakfast at Mustafa'nın Kahvaltı Dünyası, Hasan Paşa Hanı
new.desc: Fodor's lists Mustafa'nın Kahvaltı ve Yemek Dünyası inside the historic Hasan Paşa Han among the city's best breakfast options. The Diyarbakır spread brings cheeses, honey, kaymak, eggs and tandır bread.
new.tip: Go early on weekends; table space in the han fills up.
new.q: Mustafa'nın Kahvaltı Dünyası, Hasan Paşa Hanı, Dabanoğlu, Sur, Diyarbakır

new.title: Eat paça soup and mumbar at Paçacı Fazıl Usta
new.desc: Paçacı Fazıl Usta in Kayapınar serves traditional Diyarbakır dishes, notably mumbar and paça çorbası.
new.tip: Paça is a morning dish, so go early; the restaurant is in the new city, a short taxi ride from Suriçi.
new.q: Paçacı Fazıl Usta, Diclekent, Kayapınar, Diyarbakır

new.title: Try Friday lamb ribs at Meşhur Kebapçı Hacı Halid
new.desc: Hacı Halid on Çiftehan Sokak off Gazi Caddesi is known for Friday lamb ribs and for Diyarbakır güveç, and is named for duvaklı pilav in local guides.
new.tip: The ribs are a Friday special; other days try the güveç.
new.q: Hacı Halid Kebap, Çiftehan Sokak, Dabanoğlu, Sur, Diyarbakır

new.title: Share kaburga dolması at Hancı Et in Kayapınar
new.desc: Hancı Et on the 75. Yol in Kayapınar serves kaburga tava and kaburga dolması, along with gerdan and incik tava, for big family tables.
new.tip: Order the dolması ahead if you can.
new.q: Hancı Et, 75. Yol, Dünya Kavşağı, Kayapınar, Diyarbakır

new.title: Eat ciğer kebab at Dağ Kapı Ciğercisi at dawn
new.desc: Dağ Kapı Ciğercisi by the north gate grills lamb liver over charcoal, a Diyarbakır breakfast, and is listed as open from early morning to 03:00.
new.tip: Liver is traditionally eaten for breakfast; order with onion, pepper and lavash.
new.q: Dağkapı Ciğercisi, Kıbrıs Caddesi, Cami Nebi, Sur, Diyarbakır

new.title: Order lahmacun at Süleyman Usta near İçkale
new.desc: Süleyman Usta on Nebioğlu Sokak in Cami Nebi is a lahmacun and pide house in the old city, close to the Nebi Mosque.
new.tip: Closed on Sundays; go before 21:00 and order lahmacun with ayran.
new.q: Süleyman Usta Şanlıurfa Lahmacun ve Pide Evi, Nebioğlu Sokak, Cami Nebi, Sur, Diyarbakır

new.title: Order burma kadayıf at Kadayıfçı Hacı Levent Usta
new.desc: Hacı Levent Usta on Hz. Süleyman Caddesi is a dessert café known for burma kadayıf, listed also for lahmacun and meftune on the city's gastronomy route.
new.tip: Burma kadayıf with pekmez or sugar syrup is the order.
new.q: Hacı Levent Kadayıf, Hz. Süleyman Caddesi, Cami Nebi, Sur, Diyarbakır

new.title: Finish with künefe at Künefeci Salih Usta in Kayapınar
new.desc: Gaziantep Künefeci Salih Usta near the Tekel junction in Kayapınar is a late-opening dessert shop known for künefe.
new.tip: Open from midday until 01:00, so it suits an after-dinner stop.
new.q: Gaziantep Künefeci Salih Usta, Mahabad Bulvarı, Medya, Kayapınar, Diyarbakır

new.title: Taste Diyarbakır watermelon at the Dağ Kapı festival
new.desc: Diyarbakır karpuzu, grown along the Tigris and on Karacadağ, is known for its huge size. The yearly watermelon festival held at Dağ Kapı Square opens with a camel procession and a heaviest-melon contest.
new.tip: Harvest runs summer to early autumn; slices are sold in the square and at market stalls.
new.q: Dağ Kapı Meydanı, Cami Nebi, Sur, Diyarbakır
